semantic.behavior: For a regular language L represented by a finite regex AST over alphabet {0,1} and a D1 input bit a, produce a regular expression denoting exactly D_a(L)={w in {0,1}* | a concatenated with w belongs to L}. Regex constructors: empty language ZERO, epsilon EPS, literal bit, union ALT, concatenation CAT, Kleene STAR. Syntactic AST equivalence not required: denoted languages must be identical. No implicit I/O, parsing control, actual SDR timing or regex-engine backtracking.

witnesses.reason: After reading first 0, only suffix 1 remains
No word beginning with 1 matched original 01
Zero can be consumed by star
Nullable star allows bit 1 to belong to right factor
Union derivative keeps only branch matching 0

falsifiers: Taking derivative of concatenation but omitting nullable(left) branch incorrectly rejects 1 in CAT(STAR(0),1).
Using character matching instead of residual language discards all possible suffixes.
Confusing AST tree identity with language equality rejects legitimate different derivative normal forms.
Declaring empty-language AST nullable makes D_a(CAT(ZERO,X)) accept any word.
equations: D_a(ZERO)=ZERO; D_a(EPS)=ZERO; D_a(LIT(b))=EPS iff a=b else ZERO
D_a(CAT(r,s))=ALT(CAT(D_a(r),s), CAT(N(r),D_a(s))) where N(r)=EPS if nullable(r) else ZERO
nullable(ZERO)=0; nullable(EPS)=1; nullable(LIT(_))=0; nullable(ALT)=OR; nullable(CAT)=AND; nullable(STAR)=1
semantic.non_equivalence_argument: Existing MATCH-CONDITIONS implements predicate/rule matching against facts, not an operator returning the full residual regular language under one input bit. UNIFY produces substitutions for term equations, not a residual automaton language. Demonstrate via exact source and executable witnesses; owner still decides primitive-vs-library.
semantic.core_library_boundary: The operator is composable using existing exact data constructors, booleans and folds; not a new control symbol (D2 only) and not proof a distinct 10-bit resident is necessary. Strong reusable library candidate, owner semantic review required before selection.
